approachQuestion.prompt:
Archive Status Streaks

Given an array status of lowercase ASCII letters, return a list of [letter,count] records for its maximal consecutive runs, in their original order. A run cannot be extended to either neighboring position with the same letter. Separate runs of the same letter must remain separate.

Example 1: status = ["a","a","b","a"] → [["a",2],["b",1],["a",1]].
Example 2: status = ["z","z","z"] → [["z",3]].
Example 3: status = [] → [].

Constraints:
0 ≤ n = status.length ≤ 200,000.
Every element is one of a–z. Do not modify status.
Counts are positive integers. Return [] for an empty input.
constraints: Every element is one of a–z. Do not modify status.
Counts are positive integers. Return [] for an empty input.

options.text: Return [] for empty input. Otherwise remember the current letter and count. On a different letter, append the completed record and start a new run. Append the final run after the scan.
options.feedback: A change closes exactly one maximal run. Explicitly emitting the final run covers the last group even without a following different letter.

options.text: Build the output while scanning. If its last record has the current letter, increment that record’s count; otherwise append a new [letter,1] record.
options.feedback: The last output record represents exactly the still-open run. This matches the same time and auxiliary-space bounds when returned storage is excluded.

options.text: Scan once and build a separate list of input indices for every consecutive run. Then convert each list to a [letter,list length] output record.
options.feedback: This correctly preserves separate runs, but the index lists retain all input positions unnecessarily. A count per open run is enough.

options.text: Count the occurrences of each letter across the entire array, then emit one record per distinct letter in first-appearance order.
options.feedback: This merges separate runs. ["a","b","a"] needs three records, while global counting emits [["a",2],["b",1]].

options.text: Remember the current letter and count. Emit a record only when the next letter differs, and return immediately after reaching the end.
options.feedback: The last run has no following change and is omitted. A single input ["z"] should produce [["z",1]], but this method returns [].

feedback.reason: A run ends at a change of letter, not at the next occurrence of that letter anywhere in the message.
details: Handle empty input separately. Count the current consecutive run, emit it when the letter changes, and emit the remaining run after the scan ends. Append records to the returned list.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For the fixed method “Close Runs and Flush the Last”, choose the tightest worst-case time and auxiliary-space pair. Let n be the number of letters. Include all output-construction time. Appending one fixed-size record has amortized constant cost, including any resizing copies. Exclude the returned list, its capacity and records from auxiliary space; include helper variables and the call stack. No recursion or hashing is used. Use a bound valid when n=0.
constraints: Every element is one of a–z. Do not modify status.
Counts are positive integers. Return [] for an empty input.

feedback.reason: Each character updates one run and causes at most one output record.
details: Each letter contributes one comparison and count update, and at most one record is emitted per letter. Amortized append includes resizing work. The output may have n records, but it is explicitly excluded; only one letter, one count and loop state remain as auxiliary storage.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: One scan and fixed helper state suffice, with an immediate empty-input return.
The option “O(n + 1) time, O(n + 1) auxiliary space.”: This counts the returned records as auxiliary space despite the stated exclusion.
The option “O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: Producing the run records requires processing the input in the worst case.
The option “O((n + 1)²) time, O(1) auxiliary space.”: No repeated shifting or prefix rebuilding occurs under the stated append model.
